statutes.act: Act Was A Discretionary Power And It Was Amenable To Judicial Review Under Article 226 Of The Constitution

facts: The appeal arises out of the judgment of the High Court rendered in the writ petition filed by the appellant.
Section 11C of the Act reads as under: '11C. Power not to recover duty of excise not levied or short-levied as a result of general practice.'

The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, direct that the whole of the duty of excise payable on such goods, or, as the case may be, the duty of excise in excess of that payable on such goods, but for the said practice, shall not be required to be paid.
The appellant is in the business of manufacturing Rosin and Turpentine.

There are two methods of manufacturing Rosin/Turpentine from Oleo Pine Resin: one method uses power in almost all processes, while the second method, commonly known as the Bhatti process, is entirely manual except for the use of power to operate the pump for lifting up the water to the storage tank.
The appellant is using the second method of manufacturing Rosin/Turpentine.

Majority of the units (about 300) are using the Bhatti method whereby use of power is confined to lifting of water to overhead tanks for condensation of Turpentine vapours collected as liquid Turpentine in tanks.

The Central Government had exempted all goods, falling under Item No.68 of erstwhile First Schedule to the Central Government Excise and Salt Act (1 of 1944) in or relation to the manufacturing of such goods where no process is ordinarily carried on with the aid of power, from the whole of the duty of excise leviable thereon.

A show cause notice dated 04.10.2004 was issued to the appellant by the Excise Department demanding duty of Rs.10,91,99,456/- on the aforesaid products manufactured by the appellant and cleared during the period 01.04.1999 to 31.08.2003.
Gurukripa had challenged the order of assessment passed in its case by filing the appeal before the Central Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal, Mumbai (for short 'CESTAT').

This Court held that the process of lifting of water into the cooling tank was integrally connected with the manufacture of these goods and hence, if the power was used for lifting of water, the exemption would not be available.
In view of the aforesaid judgment rendered in the case of Gurukripa Resins Private Limited, appeals filed by the appellant before the CESTAT came to be dismissed.
The Central Board of Excise and Customs decided to float a survey to ascertain a general practice during the period from 27.05.1994 to 27.02.2006.
issues: Whether Section 11C of the Act grants a discretionary power to the Government to issue or not to issue such a notification.

Whether the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, direct that the whole of the duty of excise payable on such goods, or, as the case may be, the duty of excise in excess of that payable on such goods, but for the said practice, shall not be required to be paid.
petitioner_arguments: The appellant argued that Section 11C of the Act grants a discretionary power to the Government to issue or not to issue such a notification.
The appellant contended that there was a general practice of non-levying excise duty on these products during the period from 27.05.1994 to 27.02.2006.
respondent_arguments: The respondent argued that Section 11C of the Act does not mandate the Government to necessarily issue such a notification.
The respondent contended that there was no general practice of non-levying excise duty on these products during the period from 27.05.1994 to 27.02.2006.
court_reasoning: The Court held that Section 11C of the Act grants a discretionary power to the Government to issue or not to issue such a notification.
The Court observed that there was no general practice of non-levying excise duty on these products during the period from 27.05.1994 to 27.02.2006.
holding: The final decision is that the appeal is allowed and the impugned judgment of the High Court is set aside.

The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, direct that the whole of the duty of excise payable on such goods, or, as the case may be, the duty of excise in excess of that payable on such goods, but for the said practice, shall not be required to be paid.
